problems.title: Distances to parallel lines
problems.question: A point has distances 2.3 and 3.8 cm from two parallel lines. Which listed distance between the lines is possible?
problems.idea: Use the stated relation, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: The line separation is either the sum or the absolute difference of the point’s distances.
steps: If the point lies between the lines, separation is $2.3+3.8=6.1$. If it lies outside, separation is $3.8-2.3=1.5$.
Only 6.1 occurs among the choices.
problems.note: The source header calls this a summary paper dated 5 March 2021; its existing Quiz 01 archive placement is retained.

problems.title: A nested fraction
problems.question: Evaluate $1+1/(1+2/(1+3))$.
problems.idea: Use the stated relation, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: Evaluate inner parentheses before outer operations.
steps: The whole value is $1+1/(3/2)=1+2/3=5/3$.

problems.title: Percentages of supplementary angles
problems.question: 10% of one adjacent supplementary angle equals 20% of the other. Find the smaller angle.
problems.idea: Use the stated relation, then simplify and check the result.
steps: The percentage equation gives $A=2B$. Thus $3B=180^\circ$ and the smaller angle is $60^\circ$.

problems.title: Count divisors using prime exponents
problems.question: How many positive divisors does $12^3\cdot4^3$ have?
problems.idea: Use the stated relation, then simplify and check the result.
steps: A divisor chooses an exponent 0 through 12 for 2 and 0 through 3 for 3. There are $13\cdot4=52$ choices.

problems.title: An oblique segment at forty-five degrees
problems.question: $A$ lies on a line, $BK$ is perpendicular to it, $BK=5$, and $AB$ makes $45^\circ$ with the line. Find $AK$.
problems.idea: Use the stated relation, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: A right triangle with one $45^\circ$ angle is isosceles.
steps: Triangle $ABK$ has angles $45^\circ,45^\circ,90^\circ$, so its legs $AK$ and $BK$ are equal.

problems.title: Elements in one set but not the other
problems.question: $|A|=18,|B|=12,|A\cup B|=21$. Find $|A\setminus B|$.
problems.idea: Use the stated relation, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: $A\cup B$ is the disjoint union of $B$ and $A\setminus B$.
steps: $|A\setminus B|=|A\cup B|-|B|=21-12=9$.

problems.title: Mean of consecutive natural numbers
problems.question: Find the arithmetic mean of $1,2,\ldots,20$.
problems.idea: Use the stated relation, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: The mean of consecutive integers is $(\text{first}+\text{last})/2$.
steps: Pair the first and last terms: every pair totals 21. The mean is $21/2=10.5$.

problems.title: Expand a binomial cube
problems.question: Expand $(2x-1)^3$.
problems.idea: Use the stated relation, then simplify and check the result.
steps: Substitute $u=2x,v=1$: $8x^3-12x^2+6x-1$.

problems.title: A bisector in an isosceles triangle
problems.question: $AB=BC$, apex angle $B=36^\circ$, and $AK$ bisects $A$ with $K\in BC$. If $BK=12$, find base $AC$.
problems.idea: Use the stated relation, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: Equal triangle angles face equal sides; triangle angles total $180^\circ$.
steps: The base angles are $72^\circ$. In $ABK$, angles $A,B$ are both $36^\circ$, so $AK=BK=12$.
In $AKC$, angles $C,K$ are both $72^\circ$, so $AC=AK=12$.

problems.title: Angle between a right triangle’s median and altitude
problems.question: A right triangle’s acute angles differ by $20^\circ$. Find the angle between the median and altitude from the right vertex.
problems.idea: Use the stated relation, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: With legs on coordinate axes, the median direction has angle $\theta$ and the altitude direction $90^\circ-\theta$.
steps: The two acute angles are $55^\circ,35^\circ$. The median and altitude directions have these same two angle measures relative to a leg.
The angle between them is $55^\circ-35^\circ=20^\circ$.

problems.title: Two exterior angle bisectors
problems.question: $B=28^\circ$ in triangle $ABC$. Find the smaller angle between the exterior bisectors at $A,C$.
problems.idea: Use the stated relation, then simplify and check the result.
steps: The exterior bisectors at $A,C$ meet at that excenter. Their smaller angle is $90^\circ-14^\circ=76^\circ$.

problems.title: Integer lengths allowed by triangle inequalities
problems.question: Triangle sides are 7.9,23.8 and integer $n$. How many $n$ are possible?
problems.idea: Use the stated relation, then simplify and check the result.
steps: $15.9<n<31.7$. The integers are 16 through 31, for $31-16+1=16$ values.

problems.title: An exterior angle of a right isosceles triangle
problems.question: A right triangle has two sides of length 2. Which listed exterior angle can it have?
problems.idea: Use the stated relation, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: The hypotenuse is strictly longer than a leg; an exterior angle supplements its adjacent interior angle.
steps: The equal sides must be the legs, giving acute angles $45^\circ$ each.
An exterior angle at an acute vertex is $180^\circ-45^\circ=135^\circ$, which is listed.

problems.title: Compare polynomial coefficients
problems.question: $9x^2+bx+16=(3x-c)^2$ for all real $x$. Find $|b+c|$.
problems.idea: Use the stated relation, then simplify and check the result.
steps: Coefficient comparison gives $c^2=16$, so $c=\pm4$, and $b=-6c$.
Thus $|b+c|=|-5c|=20$ for either sign.

problems.title: A telescoping polynomial product
problems.question: Expand $(1-x)(1+x+x^2+x^3+x^4)$.
problems.idea: Use the stated relation, then simplify and check the result.
steps: The first product contains powers 0 through 4; the second subtracts powers 1 through 5. All intermediate powers cancel.

problems.title: Cancel equal quadratic terms
problems.question: Solve $x(12-x)-5=4x-x(10-(4-x))$.
problems.idea: Use the stated relation, then simplify and check the result.
steps: Expand to $12x-x^2-5=-2x-x^2$. Cancel $-x^2$ from both sides.

problems.title: Complete the square for a minimum
problems.question: Find the minimum of $9x^2+24x-1$.
problems.idea: Use the stated relation, then simplify and check the result.
steps: The square is nonnegative, so the expression is at least $-17$. Equality holds at $x=-4/3$.

problems.title: A hypotenuse median and the shorter leg
problems.question: A right triangle has a $30^\circ$ angle and median to its hypotenuse 8. Find its shorter leg.
problems.idea: Use the stated relation, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: The hypotenuse median is half the hypotenuse; the side opposite $30^\circ$ is also half the hypotenuse.
steps: The hypotenuse is 16. The shorter leg is $16/2=8$.

problems.title: Recover three angles from a difference and exterior angle
problems.question: Two triangle angles differ by $24^\circ$; the exterior angle at the third vertex is $124^\circ$. Find the middle-sized angle.
problems.idea: Use the stated relation, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.
steps: The first two angles have sum 124 and difference 24, so they are 74 and 50 degrees.
The third is $180-124=56$ degrees, which is between 50 and 74.

problems.title: A transversal of two parallel lines
problems.question: In the source diagram, $a\parallel b$ and $\alpha+\beta=276^\circ$. Find $x$.
problems.idea: Use the stated relation, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: Corresponding obtuse angles are equal; adjacent angles supplement each other.
steps: The diagram gives $\alpha=\beta=138^\circ$. Angle $x$ supplements $\beta$, so $x=180^\circ-138^\circ=42^\circ$.

problems.title: A sum of two distances attains its minimum
problems.question: How many real solutions does $|x-1.8|+|x-5.2|=3.4$ have?
problems.idea: Use the stated relation, then simplify and check the result.
formulas: For $a<b$, $|x-a|+|x-b|\ge b-a$, with equality iff $a\le x\le b$.
steps: Here $5.2-1.8=3.4$. Every $x$ in $[1.8,5.2]$ makes the sum exactly 3.4.
This interval contains infinitely many real numbers.
